study.citation: Stewart KM (2001) The commercial bark harvest of the African cherry (Prunus africana) on Mount Oku, Cameroon (PhD thesis); matrices as archived in COMPADRE
study.site: Mount Oku, Cameroon (per thesis; COMPADRE plot labels only)
study.notes: One unharvested plot vs four harvested plots (once or twice per year), 1997-1999. No DOI; single control plot means the contrast has no replication on the control side. The thesis abstract reports lambda below 1 in harvested plots; 6 of 8 single-year harvested matrices here are below 1, but the 1997-99 mean matrices used for this comparison are at or above 1 in 3 of 4 plots. A later forest-wide harvest (2005/06) is outside these matrices (Stewart 2009, For Ecol Manage 258:1121).
study.citation_source: COMPADRE metadata (no DOI; thesis/grey literature, not independently verified)

design_caveat: Harvested vs unharvested populations differ in site/period too: contrast is not a causal effect estimate.
n0_basis: stable stage distribution × 100 (hypothetical; normalised index, not a local stock)
